office.body: Our Evanston office is at 1603 Orrington Ave, #600-1085, Evanston, IL 60201, in downtown Evanston. It keeps our plumbers close to homes across Evanston and the neighboring North Shore communities. We’ve served Chicagoland homeowners since 1993, and our phone line is open 24/7.

depth.h2: What Evanston Homes Need From a Plumber
depth.intro: The median home in Evanston was built in 1953, and about 4 in 10 were built before 1940. The city’s own sewers are 80 to more than 100 years old. That history shows up in almost every plumbing call we take here.

tiles.title: Older Homes, Older Sewer Lines
tiles.body: The line from your house to the city sewer belongs to you, and in an older Evanston home it’s often clay or cast iron. Roots get in at the joints, and sections crack or sag. A [camera inspection](/evanston/video-camera-sewer-inspections) shows the condition of your line before you decide on a [sewer repair](/evanston/sewer-repair).

tiles.title: A Combined Sewer City
tiles.body: All of Evanston is served by a combined sewer system, which carries rainwater and wastewater in the same pipes. The city built relief sewers between 1991 and 2008, but a basement can still back up from an overloaded sewer or a blocked line. A [backflow valve](/evanston/flood-control-maintenance) or an [overhead sewer](/evanston/overhead-sewer-systems) keeps sewer water out.

tiles.title: Catch Basins That Back Up
tiles.body: Many Evanston yards and driveways drain into a catch basin. When leaves and silt fill it, rainwater has nowhere to go and pools against the foundation. We [clean and repair catch basins](/evanston/catch-basin) and clear the line they drain into.

tiles.title: Hard Water and Water Heaters
tiles.body: Evanston treats its own Lake Michigan water, and the city’s latest water report puts the average hardness at about 7.8 grains per gallon. That counts as hard water, and it builds scale in a water heater over the years. When a heater starts to rumble, leak or run out fast, we can [repair or replace it](/evanston/water-heater-repair).

items.q: How much does a plumber cost in Evanston?
items.a: It depends on the job. The main factors are what’s wrong, how hard it is to reach, the parts or materials needed and the age of your plumbing. Work in an older home with original pipe can take more time than a newer one. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins, so you know the cost going in.

items.q: How fast can you get to my home in an emergency?
items.preview: Call us any time, day or night, including weekends and holidays.
items.a: Call us any time, day or night, including weekends and holidays. Our Orrington Avenue office keeps our plumbers close to every part of Evanston, and we [treat emergencies as a priority](/evanston/emergency-plumbing). Arrival times depend on the day, but we’ll get a plumber to you as soon as we can.

items.q: My kitchen sink drain keeps clogging. What can you do?
items.preview: We clear the line, not just the trap.
items.a: We clear the line, not just the trap. Grease and food build up inside kitchen drain pipes over the years, especially in older homes, and a quick plunge only moves the clog. We [clean the kitchen line](/evanston/drain-cleaning#kitchen-sink-drain) back to the stack and tell you if the pipe itself needs work.

items.q: Who is responsible for the sewer line in Evanston?
items.preview: The property owner is responsible for the line from the house to the city sewer, including the section under the parkway.
items.a: The property owner is responsible for the line from the house to the city sewer, including the section under the parkway. If a camera inspection shows the problem is in the city sewer, we’ll tell you so you can report it.

items.q: Why did my basement back up during a storm?
items.preview: Evanston’s sewers carry rainwater and wastewater in the same pipes.
items.a: Evanston’s sewers carry rainwater and wastewater in the same pipes. In a heavy storm, the system can fill up and push water back toward the lowest drain in your house. A partly blocked lateral makes it worse. We can clear and camera your line and recommend a backflow valve or overhead sewer.

items.q: How often should a catch basin be cleaned?
items.preview: Once a year for most homes, usually after the leaves fall.
items.a: Once a year for most homes, usually after the leaves fall. If you have big trees nearby or water pools near the basin after rain, it may need it more often.

hub.ndc: Most plumbing problems in Evanston start small, like roots in an old clay sewer line or a catch basin full of leaves. The [No Drip Club](/no-drip-club) brings a plumber to your home for regular maintenance, so issues get caught early.

final.h2: Your Evanston Plumber, Day or Night
final.body: Small leaks and slow drains don’t fix themselves. Call us early, and we’ll keep a small problem from turning into a big one.
